question.worked_solution:
Substituting $x=\dfrac{\pi}{8}$ directly into the limit, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \pi /8}{(1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))}^{2} & ={(1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8}))}^{2} \\  & ={(1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}))}^{2} \\  & ={(1+2\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2} \\  & ={(1+\sqrt{2})}^{2} \\  & ={1}^{2}+2\cdot 1\cdot \sqrt{2}+{(\sqrt{2})}^{2} \\  & =1+2\sqrt{2}+2 \\  & =3+2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
